title: Pope's The Rape of the Lock: mock-epic and a stolen curl

right.title: Mock-epic

explain.say: Around 1711, at a fashionable party, a young lord snipped a lock of hair from a young woman, Arabella Fermor, and their families fell out. Alexander Pope was asked to laugh them back together. In the title, rape means seizing, from Latin, the theft of the curl. The board shows his trick: mock-epic.

explain.say: Mock-epic takes the grand style of Homer and uses it for something tiny. Follow Belinda's panels. Look at the second: she sits at her dressing table, and her make-up is described like a hero putting on armour before battle. Why does that make you smile?

explain.say: Pope writes in heroic couplets, rhyming pairs of iambic pentameter. His favourite joke is zeugma, yoking a grand thing and a trivial one with the same verb. Look at the sort: Queen Anne sometimes takes counsel, and sometimes tea. Can you make one?

explain.say: The lock is never found. In the last panel it rises into the sky as a new star, and the poem itself makes Belinda immortal. Brilliant. Exam tip: name the epic convention, then show what trivial thing replaces it. Challenge: write a mock-epic couplet about losing your phone.

faq.q: What does rape mean in The Rape of the Lock?
faq.a: It means seizing or carrying off, from the Latin rapere. The title refers to the theft of a lock of Belinda's hair, in mock-heroic style.
asks: Why is it called The Rape of the Lock?

faq.a: A poem that applies the grand conventions of epic, gods, battles, arming scenes, a journey to the underworld, to a trivial subject, to make fun of it.
A figure where one word governs two others in different senses, often one grand and one trivial, like stain her honour, or her new brocade.
Tiny airy spirits, led by Ariel, who guard Belinda's beauty. They parody the gods who protect heroes in epic, and Pope added them in the 1714 version.
asks: Sylphs in The Rape of the Lock

faq.q: What real event inspired The Rape of the Lock?
faq.a: Lord Petre cut a lock of Arabella Fermor's hair, causing a quarrel between two Catholic families. Pope's friend John Caryll asked him to write a poem to calm it.

facts: The first version of The Rape of the Lock (1712) had two cantos; the 1714 version had five.
Pope wrote the poem in heroic couplets.
